title: Recollecting virtue
hook: a robe is being sewn for a journey, and a lay follower asks how to live once the teacher is gone
tomorrow: how can giving something away be a gain for you?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the third jewel: the community, practicing well. The Buddha, the teaching, the community. Now the list turns around and points at you.

A going-away gift says the thing nobody wants to say out loud: someone is leaving. In one sutta, monks are sewing a new robe for the Buddha, and a finished robe means he'll soon set out walking. Mahanama the Sakyan, a lay follower, hears about the sewing and understands. He comes with the question under all those needles. We who live in all sorts of ways, with houses and work and families: when you go, how should we live? The answer begins with three names anyone would expect. Then it does something strange. It tells Mahanama to remember himself.
screen: `A GOING-AWAY GIFT.` → `A ROBE FOR THE ROAD.` → `HOW SHOULD WE LIVE?`

segments.voice: The Buddha gives Mahanama things to call to mind. The Buddha. The teaching. The community. And fourth: your own virtue. Not a saint's. Yours. Recall the precepts you've kept, he says, kept whole, unbroken, unstained, the kind the wise would praise. Then he lays out what happens next, like a chain. When you remember that, the mind isn't taken over by greed, or hate, or confusion. It goes straight. Gladness comes, and out of gladness, joy. The body calms. A calm body feels at ease, and a mind at ease settles. Buddhaghosa's meditation manual, the Visuddhimagga, turns this into a subject of its own: sit, and go over your conduct gladly. That last word does the work. This isn't a résumé, and nobody else needs to hear it. It's closer to the quiet at the end of a day when you told the truth and it cost you something. The texts are speaking to someone whose conduct is clean. If yours has a smudge, one answer in the tradition is plain: take the precepts again, keep them, and then there's something to remember. Glad of my conduct, and no trace of showing off.
screen: `THE BUDDHA, THE TEACHING, THE COMMUNITY.` · `FOURTH: YOUR OWN VIRTUE.` · `THE MIND GOES STRAIGHT.` · `GLADLY, NOT TO SHOW OFF.` · then, large: `GLAD OF MY CONDUCT.`

segments.voice: Find one time you did the decent thing when it would have been easier not to: the truth told, the wallet handed back, the cruel joke you didn't make. Write it as one short line, on paper if you have some, and rest your eyes on that line for the sit. If gladness comes, let it stay; if it doesn't, the remembering is enough.
Recollecting virtue: calling your own good conduct to mind, gladly, as a meditation. The fourth thing the Buddha told Mahanama to remember.
Hold on to this: glad of my conduct, the quiet kind of glad. Twenty-two days into the forty subjects.

screen: `DAY 1527 COUNTS.` → `FORTY SUBJECTS · 22 OF 40.` → `TOMORROW: HOW IS GIVING AWAY A GAIN?`

howItsDone: Lay Buddhists take the five precepts at temple gatherings and on observance days, and Theravada teachers give the recollection of virtue as a quiet meditation on precepts kept.

fork.setup: you kept a hard promise to a friend, and you keep replaying it at night, quietly glad. someone says that's just ego. what does the manual say?

fork.reveal: the Visuddhimagga makes this a meditation: go over your conduct gladly. the chain runs from gladness to joy, calm, ease and a settled mind.

original.note: Pali: sila, virtue or conduct, with anussati, recollection, calling to mind.

trapdoor: what you thought: patting yourself on the back.
what it means: going over your own kept precepts, privately and gladly, until the mind goes straight and settles.
what a scholar hears: it's the fourth of six recollections the Buddha gives Mahanama (AN 11.11; also AN 6.10), and Visuddhimagga 7 sets it out as a meditation subject.

chat.says: art program app asks for 'a moment you're proud of.' bragging feels gross. blank screen for an hour.
options: Remembering what you did right isn't bragging. Say it plainly, gladly, and let it be true.
Pick a time someone else praised you instead; then it isn't your own claim.
Write about a mistake instead. Dwelling on your own good is always a bit vain.
chat.meaning: Recollecting virtue means calling your own good conduct to mind, gladly. It's private and settling, not showing off.

tie.story: The Buddha told Mahanama to remember his own kept precepts, gladly, until the mind goes straight.
tie.friend: Mai can name one real thing she did well, plainly, without dressing it up.
tie.you: what's one decent thing you did that you could remember gladly?

Mahanama.meaning: a lay follower of the Sakyan clan who asked how to live

Visuddhimagga.meaning: Buddhaghosa's meditation manual: the path of purification

Buddhaghosa.meaning: the monk-scholar who wrote the Visuddhimagga

precepts.meaning: the basic promises of conduct a Buddhist undertakes

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 11.11 (Mahanama Sutta: the robe being made; Mahanama asks how to dwell; six recollections, the fourth being one's own virtue)
Anguttara Nikaya 6.10 (recollecting virtue: unbroken, untorn, praised by the wise; the mind goes straight; gladness, joy, calm, ease, concentration)

notes: Story shape: the hook is the scene in AN 11.11 (the robe being sewn before the Buddha sets out; Mahanama asks how lay followers should live). Confirm the scene and that virtue is the fourth recollection there.
The chain (mind not overcome by greed, hatred, delusion; goes straight; gladness, joy, bodily calm, ease, concentration) paraphrased from AN 6.10 / AN 11.11. Confirm.
'One answer in the tradition: take the precepts again' is a general description (the Visuddhimagga addresses a practitioner whose virtue is purified). Confirm the framing.
Kept the index word exactly (the title's head); the Pali silanussati is in games.original only.
